messages:
maria: Hey folks, customer on enterprise Dedicated reports embeddings endpoint returning inconsistent vector sizes when using our Go SDK with batching + retries. They see 512 expected but sometimes get 1536.

alex: Oof. Do we have a repro? Which model / batch sizes / SDK version?

maria: Repro from the customer: Go SDK v0.9.4, model: rwd-embed-large (512-dim). They batch 4 inputs and have a retry/backoff wrapper. Intermittent: one of the items in the batch returns 1536-length vector in the response payload, others are correct.

maria: Paste of minimal repro (redacted keys):
```go
ctx := context.Background()
client := redwood.NewClient("REDACTED_API_KEY")
inputs := []string{"a", "b", "c", "d"}
resp, err := client.Embeddings.Create(ctx, &redwood.EmbeddingsRequest{
    Model: "rwd-embed-large",
    Input: inputs,
})
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for i, v := range resp.Data {
    fmt.Println(i, len(v.Embedding))
}
```

maria: Output they saw on failing run: 0 512
1 512
2 1536
3 512

samir: Any raw HTTP logs? headers / request ids? Could be a client-side buffer reuse or a server-side path that concatenates multiple embeddings when retrying a partially completed streaming response.

maria: Customer provided server logs excerpt (sanitized):
```
2026-11-02T14:22:11Z req_id=cr-87a1 qid=01A accept=application/json body_bytes=2048 batching_key=batch-927
2026-11-02T14:22:11Z handler=embed process_ms=9 status=200 resp_size=6144 model=rwd-embed-large seq=0
2026-11-02T14:22:11Z handler=embed process_ms=11 status=200 resp_size=6144 model=rwd-embed-large seq=1
2026-11-02T14:22:11Z handler=embed process_ms=47 status=200 resp_size=18432 model=rwd-embed-large seq=2
2026-11-02T14:22:11Z handler=embed process_ms=8 status=200 resp_size=6144 model=rwd-embed-large seq=3
```

maria: Note resp_size for seq=2 is ~3x, matches 3x512 vectors concatenated into one item (1536).

alex: Hmm, looks like a correlation bug where a retried subrequest's data got merged into subsequent item. Does the Go SDK reuse a single byte buffer for streaming responses across items?

ryan: I dug into the Go SDK 0.9.4 embedding path earlier this week. There's a pooling path that reuses a bytes.Buffer from a sync.Pool for JSON decoding to reduce allocations. If a retry occurs and the buffer isn't zeroed properly before parsing, I could see concat artifacts.

ingrid: Customer says they have a retry wrapper that retries the entire batch on 5xx and implements exponential backoff. Retries were triggered once in their run (transient 502 between seq 1 and 2).

samir: If the server returns partial success for individual items (we currently return 200 for completed items in the batch and 202 for pending?), we might be merging per-item payloads when reconstructing a retried response. But the logs show status=200 for each seq. Could be client merging two different responses into one slot.

maria: I asked customer to reproduce with single-threaded run (no parallelism) and to attach full HTTP exchange. They sent the following captured response body (pretty-printed):
```json
{
  "data": [
    {"embedding": [/*512 floats*/]},
    {"embedding": [/*512 floats*/]},
    {"embedding": [/*512 floats*/ , /*512 floats*/, /*512 floats*/]},
    {"embedding": [/*512 floats*/]}
  ],
  "model": "rwd-embed-large",
  "usage": {"input_tokens": 42}
}
```

alex: That matches the resp_size anomaly. So the server response for item 2 contains three embeddings collapsed into one array. Does our server ever append multiple embeddings into one array element? No. So either client mis-indexes the parsed arrays or server-sided proxy is duplicating chunks.

ryan: Quick check: Go SDK decoder decodes into []EmbeddingStruct then assigns into resp.Data. There's a loop that does: for i := range decoded { resp.Data[i].Embedding = decoded[i].Embedding } — if decoded length > resp.Data cap, that could index-shift. But decoded is created directly from JSON.Unmarshal, so lengths should align. The pooling bug could leave trailing floats in the same slice if we reuse slices without resetting length/capacity properly.

maria: Customer also tried TS SDK (ts-sdk v1.2.0) and Python (py-sdk v0.12.0) with same batch size + retries; they did NOT see the issue there. Only Go SDK.

samir: So root cause likely in Go client. Action plan: 1) Ask infra to check any proxy that could conflate responses (quick double-check). 2) Run unit test on Go SDK: repeated batch calls with artificial 502 then success and ensure no cross-contamination. 3) Patch Go SDK to avoid slice reuse on decode or ensure deep copy after decode. 4) Recommend temp customer mitigation: disable client-side retries or set max_retries=0 and use per-item retries, or set batch_size=1 until we patch.

maria: I've tried to reproduce locally by simulating a retry: forced 502 then success; I can repro intermittent 1536-length vector 2/30 runs. I captured the decoded slice header: cap and len show cap enough to hold 1536 but len shows 512; however print of underlying array shows concatenated floats. So it's slice header reuse with append behavior.

ryan: Proposed minimal fix: after Unmarshal into temp var 'decoded', for each d := range decoded { resp.Data[i].Embedding = append([]float64(nil), d.Embedding...) } — ensures copy. We'll ship as 0.9.5 with a test. Lower perf but safe. Also look at using encoding/json.Decoder.Decode into freshly allocated structures rather than reusing pooled buffers for the slice elements.

ingrid: For customer comms: offer a rollback to older Go SDK (0.8.x) or ask them to set SDK env REDWOOD_EMB_GO_BUFFER_POOL=0 to disable pooling (we can add this knob). Otherwise suggest batch_size=1 as emergency mitigation.

support-bot: Created ticket INC-2026-4536 and attached manifests + logs. Assigned to eng-ml (ryan) / eng (alex). ETA requested: asap/patch in 24-48h.

alex: Can you open a small PR with the append-copy fix and add unit tests that simulate a retry with swapped responses? Keep test deterministic by using the same buffer pool sequence.

ryan: Will do. Also adding instrumentation: if we detect embedding length != model_dim, log the request_id and dump raw decoded json to S3 (redacted) for faster triage.

maria: Customer confirmed they can disable retries for now and will try 0.9.5 once available. I'll follow up in 24h with their status. Thanks team :thumbsup:

ryan: filing PR now -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/412 (WIP)

maria: Marking thread for follow-up. If anyone else sees embed dim anomalies in other languages, ping me.
